recommendedTextbook.title: Basic Civic Education for Junior Secondary Schools 2
recommendedTextbook.author: M.O. Adebayo, S.A. Falade, E.O. Ajibola

topics.topic: Integrity and Moral Courage in Public and Private Life
subtopics: Definition of integrity as steadfast adherence to moral and ethical principles
Attributes of integrity: accountability, probity, moral courage, resisting bribery
People of integrity in Nigerian history (e.g. Chief Gani Fawehinmi, Dora Akunyili)
objectives: Define integrity and contrast it with opportunistic compromise
Evaluate case studies of ethical whistleblowing in Nigerian regulatory agencies

topics.topic: Discipline and Contentment: Virtues for a Corrupt-Free Nigeria
subtopics: Meaning of discipline (self-control, obedience to rules without supervision)
Meaning and attributes of contentment (satisfaction with honest earnings, avoiding greed)
Negative effects of lack of contentment: cybercrime (yahoo-yahoo), armed robbery, fraud
objectives: Explain how contentment shields youth from criminal get-rich-quick peer pressures
Formulate personal codes of conduct for academic and digital integrity

topics.topic: Courage: Types, Attributes and Demonstration in Daily Life
subtopics: Meaning of courage (ability to stand for what is right despite fear or intimidation)
Types of courage: physical courage vs moral courage vs spiritual courage
Demonstrating moral courage against school bullying and exam malpractice
objectives: Differentiate physical courage from moral courage with relatable secondary school examples
Role-play reporting an injustice to school authorities with moral firmness

topics.topic: The Rule of Law: Equality Before the Law and Due Process
subtopics: A.V. Dicey's principles of the Rule of Law: supremacy of regular law, equality before the law, fundamental human liberties
Due process in legal arrest, detention, and trial in Nigerian courts
Factors that hinder the Rule of Law: executive lawlessness, judicial corruption, delay in justice delivery
objectives: State the three cardinal pillars of the Rule of Law formulated by A.V. Dicey
Explain why no citizen or public official is above the law in a constitutional democracy

topics.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the 1948 UDHR Declaration
subtopics: History and adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) by the United Nations in 1948
Seven core categories of human rights (civil, political, economic, social, cultural rights)
Agencies protecting human rights in Nigeria: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), Legal Aid Council
objectives: Cite major articles of the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Explain how the National Human Rights Commission investigates abuses in Nigeria

topics.topic: Consumer Rights and Protection Agencies: FCCPC, NAFDAC & SON
subtopics: Consumer rights: right to safety, right to be informed, right to choose, right to redress
Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) mandates
NAFDAC (regulation of processed food, cosmetics, drugs) and SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria for manufactured goods)
objectives: Inspect product packaging for NAFDAC registration numbers, manufacturing dates, and expiry dates
Outline steps for filing a formal consumer complaint to the FCCPC over defective goods

subtopics: Evaluation on integrity, contentment, courage, rule of law, human rights, and consumer rights
Interactive human rights debate
objectives: Assess pupil performance against JSS 2 Civic Education standards

topics.topic: Emergency Management in Nigeria: NEMA and Disaster Preparedness
subtopics: Definition of disasters: natural disasters (flooding, windstorms) vs man-made disasters (fire, building collapse, pipeline explosion)
Establishment and roles of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and State Emergency Management Agencies (SEMA)
Emergency phone numbers and school fire evacuation drills
objectives: Differentiate natural disasters from preventable man-made disasters in Nigeria
Describe NEMA's search, rescue, and relief operations during flood emergencies

topics.topic: Cultism in Schools: Dangers, Prevention and Legal Sanctions
subtopics: Meaning and historical origin of secret cults in Nigerian tertiary and secondary institutions
Causes of youth involvement in cultism: search for power, peer pressure, intimidation, false protection
Consequences: violence, loss of life, expulsion from school, criminal imprisonment under state anti-cultism laws
objectives: Explain why secondary school students must reject invitations to secret cult gatherings
Outline severe legal and academic sanctions enacted against cult membership in Nigeria

topics.topic: Drug and Substance Abuse: Roles of NDLEA and NAFDAC
subtopics: Meaning of drug abuse: using prescription drugs without a doctor's prescription or consuming illicit substances
Commonly abused substances: tramadol, codeine cough syrups, cannabis (marijuana), Colorado, synthetic narcotics
Health and social hazards: psychosis, organ failure, crime; statutory roles of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
objectives: List physical, psychological, and social effects of substance abuse on Nigerian adolescents
Describe NDLEA's interdiction and rehabilitation programs across the 36 states

topics.topic: Leadership and Followership in Democratic Governance
subtopics: Qualities of an effective democratic leader: visionary, accountable, empathetic, communicative
Qualities of constructive followers: law-abiding, constructive criticism, active civic participation
Role-playing executive leadership in school prefect councils
objectives: Contrast democratic leadership with autocratic and laissez-faire leadership styles
Formulate a manifesto for a student representative council election

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & Civic Values Clinic
subtopics: Review of integrity, rule of law, NEMA, cultism prevention, and leadership
Classroom civic ethics mock tribunal
objectives: Complete JSS 2 Civic Education Term 1 syllabus review

subtopics: Terminal examination and grading
objectives: Complete JSS 2 Civic Education evaluation
